summary: Security fix (столп 4): the report-page endpoints computed/dumped record data over the WHOLE registry gated ONLY by an application-level READ grant (checkReadGrant), never a record-level READ-PDP check — so a narrow record-scope actor received data/aggregates over rows they cannot read individually. TWO sibling surfaces of the same wall: (1) /render + /export (Floor-1 aggregate, buildAggSql) computed SUM/AVG/COUNT/MIN/MAX/LIST over EVERY record — the defect adversary-skeptic T-0587 found and ADR-T0587 §1.1 explicitly declined to fix. (2) /data (dataFloor2, LEAK A found by adversary opus on review of the first T-0632 iteration) dumped the FULL data of EVERY record + an exact full-registry COUNT(*) — the raw-row twin of the aggregate leak. T-0632 closes BOTH at the source: variant (б) — a per-row isRecordReadable filter over a bounded raw-row fetch. For aggregates the visible subset is folded in application code (new pure module src/core/visible-record-agg.ts, full Floor-1 vocab); for /data the raw dump is filtered to visible records and total_count is the VISIBLE count (not SELECT COUNT(*)). Same discipline the analyst chat (T-0587) and GET /api/records (T-0570) already use. The application-level checkReadGrant remains the first, mandatory gate; the record-level filter is an additional, second gate on top. Also audited /process-analytics (4th route): reads the S3 transition journal, not choros.record — not a record-scope READ-PDP surface, no change needed.

fix_variant.chosen: б — per-row isRecordReadable filter over a bounded raw-row fetch; aggregate computed in application code over the visible subset only
fix_variant.why: Gives an HONEST sum over VISIBLE records (matches T-0587's analyst-chat behavior) rather than an all-or-nothing deny (variant а, rejected — would turn any partially-visible registry into a hard refusal, less useful than a correct partial sum) or a full-registry-coverage gate (variant в, rejected — a narrow-but-nonempty grant is a legitimate T-0570 scenario, e.g. FF-RP-5's 'narrow-actor sees record1 ONLY'; requiring full coverage to answer at all is less honest than answering with the true visible subset). A SQL-side scope-containment predicate (materializing isNarrowerOrEqual as SQL) was also considered and rejected — it would duplicate the TS authority math in SQL, a second implementation of the same decision (NF-1 violation risk of divergence). Full reasoning + rejected-alternatives table: docs/design/ADR-T0632-report-agg-readpdp.md §2.1 and §4.

mechanism.resolver: New optional export ReportAggReadVisibilityResolver on src/http/report-page-render.ts, wired unconditionally in src/server.ts (grantsPool-gated) with the BYTE-IDENTICAL composition already used by registerRecordRoutes's resolveReadVisibility (src/server.ts:875-885): getGrantsForSubject(grantsPool, tenantId, actorSlug, nowMs) + loadTenantOrgAncestry(grantsPool, tenantId) → makeResourceAncestryOracle(orgOracle, emptyRowIndex). Single-resolver (NF-1) — no new authority store, no new ACL, no second implementation of grant-lattice math.
mechanism.row_filter: renderFloor1 resolves { grants, ancestry } ONCE per render call (not per row/metric — mirrors records.ts's per-request resolve). For each metric, buildRawRecordSql fetches a BOUNDED (AGG_SCAN_LIMIT=5000) window of raw {id, data} rows (same tenant/registry/filter WHERE predicate + charset+whitelist guards as the old SQL aggregate). Each row is filtered through isRecordReadable(rowAncestry, grants, ancestry, nowMs) — the EXACT predicate src/core/read-visibility.ts exports and GET /api/records / registry-digest-dao.ts (T-0587's analyst digest) already use. Only rows passing the predicate are folded into a new pure accumulator (VisibleAggregator, src/core/visible-record-agg.ts) which supports the FULL Floor-1 vocab (count/sum/avg/min/max/list, with group_by and filter) — a generalization of T-0587's visible-aggregate.ts (which only covered numeric count/sum/avg/min/max, no group_by/filter/list).
mechanism.honest_degrade: The resolver parameter is OPTIONAL on registerReportPageRenderRoutes/renderFloor1 (mirrors records.ts's ReadVisibilityResolver? pattern) so pre-existing unit tests that construct the router directly without a resolver keep compiling and keep exercising the OLD full-registry SQL aggregate path (retained, renamed conceptually to 'legacy/fallback', code unchanged in behavior) — this is a TEST-ONLY degradation, never a sanctioned production state; src/server.ts wires the resolver unconditionally whenever grantsPool exists (i.e. whenever DATABASE_URL is set — the only case the render path can do anything at all).
mechanism.data_endpoint_leak_a: dataFloor2 (GET /api/report-pages/:id/data) now takes the SAME resolveReadVisibility (threaded from the same registration site — the route call now passes it). When wired: (step 3b) resolve { grants, ancestry } ONCE; (default path) SELECT r.id, r.data, r.created_at, r.updated_at, rd.application_id FROM choros.record r JOIN choros.registry_def rd ... LIMIT AGG_SCAN_LIMIT (bounded candidate window, the join carries application_id for the RowAncestry the predicate walks, exactly as registry-digest-dao.ts joins it); filter each candidate through isRecordReadable; total_count = visibleRows.length (NOT SELECT COUNT(*) — a full-registry count would itself leak the exact number of hidden records); paginate the visible subset in-memory via slice(offset, offset+limit) (mirrors records.ts LIST filtering the already-loaded page). Honest-degrade (no resolver): the ORIGINAL SELECT COUNT(*) + SQL LIMIT/OFFSET full dump, byte-identical to pre-T-0632 — test-only, never production (server.ts wires the resolver). The application-level checkReadGrant remains the FIRST, mandatory gate (unchanged).

changes_requested_leak_a.finding: Adversary opus, HIGH: closing only /render + /export was insufficient — the READ-PDP hole was not walled because the sibling column /data (dataFloor2) still leaked. It did a full raw-row dump (SELECT id, data, created_at, updated_at over ALL records) + SELECT COUNT(*), gated ONLY by application-level checkReadGrant. The same narrow record-scope actor the /render fix protects could read the FULL data of EVERY record + the exact full-registry count via /data.
changes_requested_leak_a.how_closed: Threaded resolveReadVisibility into dataFloor2; per-row isRecordReadable filter over a bounded candidate window; total_count derived from the VISIBLE count (not SELECT COUNT(*)); in-memory pagination of the visible subset. Mirrors records.ts LIST (~1969-1981) byte-for-byte in intent. The /render + /export fix (visible-record-agg, runVisibilityFilteredMetric) was NOT touched.
changes_requested_leak_a.leak_b_decision: LEAK B (LOW, truncated on /render reveals a coarse >=AGG_SCAN_LIMIT pre-fetch count): ACCEPTED as-is, documented. Kept byte-identical to the already-accepted T-0587/registry-digest-dao.ts precedent (recRes.rows.length === scanLimit). Computing truncated from the visible fold-count instead would be semantically WRONG, not merely asymmetric — truncated must mean 'candidate scan window may be incomplete' (a pre-filter property), so a registry of 5000 candidates with 3 visible rows still needs the flag. It is a coarse >=5000 signal that never reveals data of a specific hidden record. Documented at the const truncated computation site + ADR-T0632 §7.
changes_requested_leak_a.full_file_audit: Enumerated ALL 4 routes + ALL choros.record queries in report-page-render.ts: /render (runVisibilityFilteredMetric → isRecordReadable, fixed prior iteration), /export (reuses renderFloor1, same filter, fixed prior iteration), /data (dataFloor2, fixed THIS iteration), /process-analytics (reads the S3 transition journal via loadCycleTimeByActivity/loadActorTypeBreakdown over audit_event — process telemetry, NOT choros.record, does not expose per-record business data; not a record-scope READ-PDP surface, consistent with T-0587 treating the S3 journal as internal telemetry — no change needed). No other report-page endpoint has raw record access bypassing READ-PDP.
changes_requested_leak_a.mutation_proof: Unit (report-page-render.test.ts, T-0632 LEAK A block): neutralizing the /data isRecordReadable filter (return true) → AC-DATA-1 failed 'expected 2 to be 1' (narrow actor saw BOTH records) and AC-DATA-2 failed 'expected 2 to be +0' (zero-grant actor saw both). DB (report-page-render-read-pdp.db.test.ts, LEAK A block, live Postgres via createServer()): same neutralization → narrow actor's /data returned BOTH record ids (the hidden record leaked) instead of only their 1 visible record. Both reverted; fix restored and reverified green.

reuse_of_t0587_mechanism: T-0632 reuses, byte-for-byte, the SAME three primitives T-0587 (analyst chat) and T-0570 (GET /api/records) already use: getGrantsForSubject (src/db/grants-dao.ts), loadTenantOrgAncestry + makeResourceAncestryOracle (src/db/org-ancestry.ts / src/db/resource-ancestry.ts), and isRecordReadable (src/core/read-visibility.ts). No new authority math was written. The NEW module (src/core/visible-record-agg.ts) is a generalization of T-0587's visible-aggregate.ts's 'pure accumulation over an already-filtered stream' pattern — visible-aggregate.ts only covered the analyst's own numeric-digest needs (count/sum/avg/min/max on ONE field, no group_by/filter/list); report-page-render.ts's Floor-1 vocab (ADR-T0121 §4) additionally needed group_by, filter, and the list aggregate, none of which visible-aggregate.ts supported — hence a new, sibling module rather than extending the frozen-by-convention T-0587 module in place.

tests.unit_new: src/core/__tests__/visible-record-agg.test.ts (19 tests, pure IO-free) — count/sum/avg/min/max/list non-grouped + grouped variants, FF-2/AC-4 order-of-filtering invariant (a row simulating isRecordReadable===false, never .fold()-ed, has ZERO effect — the huge excluded value never reaches the sum), matchesFilter for =/!=/</>/in mirroring the original SQL filter clause's TEXT-comparison semantics byte-for-byte (not a numeric 'upgrade' that would silently change which rows an existing page_def matches).
tests.unit_extended: src/__tests__/report-page-render.test.ts — TWO new describe blocks (6 tests total, FakePool-level): (A) 'T-0632 — record-level READ-PDP filtering of Floor-1 aggregates' (3 tests): AC-T0632-1 narrow record-scope grant → SUM over the visible record ONLY (never the hidden record's huge value); AC-T0632-2 zero covering record grants → count:0; AC-T0632-3 resolveReadVisibility ABSENT → legacy full-registry SQL aggregate unchanged. (B) 'T-0632 LEAK A — record-level READ-PDP filtering of Floor-2 /data raw dump' (3 tests): AC-DATA-1 narrow grant → /data returns ONLY the visible record + total_count = visible count (not full registry); AC-DATA-2 zero grants → empty records + total_count:0 (not 403/500/full dump); AC-DATA-3 resolver ABSENT → legacy full-registry dump + SELECT COUNT(*) path unchanged. All pre-existing 30 tests in this file (charset guard, schema whitelist, WRONG_FLOOR, 401/403/404, injection probes AC-1..AC-16) pass UNCHANGED — the honest-degrade fallback path they exercise (no resolver passed) preserves byte-identical legacy behavior.
tests.db_new: ci/checks/db/report-page-render-read-pdp.db.test.ts (4 tests, live Postgres, real src/server.ts createServer() composition root — same resolveReadVisibility wiring as GET /api/records): AC-T0632-1 (mutational) two real actors, one narrow record-scope grant (covers 1 of 2 records, values 100/900) and one wide grant (covers both) — narrow actor's Floor-1 SUM = 100 (never 100+900=1000), wide actor's SUM = 1000, narrowSum strictly < wideSum; AC-T0632-2 actor with application-read grant but ZERO record-level grants → count:0 on a non-empty (1-record) registry, 200 not 403/500; AC-T0632-3 genesis-owner (e-owner) is UNAFFECTED — still sees the full SUM=1000; LEAK A block — three actors (narrow record-scope, wide, zero-grant) hit GET /api/report-pages/:id/data: narrow sees ONLY record1 + total_count 1 (not 2), wide sees both + total_count 2, zero-grant sees empty records[] + total_count 0 — all 200 (application-read grant passes the page gate; record-level filter narrows the dump). Mutationally red before fix (neutralizing the /data filter → narrow actor saw both record ids).
tests.mutation_proof: Confirmed RED-before-fix on BOTH the unit and DB test suites by reverting src/http/report-page-render.ts (git show HEAD:...) with the new tests kept: unit AC-T0632-1 failed 'expected null to be 42' (old 4-arg signature silently dropped the 5th resolver arg — structurally cannot take it), and with a targeted single-line mutation (commenting out the `if (!isRecordReadable(...)) continue;` guard on the FIXED code) AC-T0632-1 failed 'expected 1000041 to be 42' (the hidden record's 999999 leaked into the sum) and AC-T0632-2 failed 'expected 2 to be +0' (both records counted). DB-level: reverting src/http/report-page-render.ts + src/server.ts to HEAD (pre-fix) reproduced the SAME class of failure against a REAL Postgres — AC-T0632-1 'expected 1000 to be 100' (narrow actor saw the FULL registry sum, the exact vulnerability) and AC-T0632-2 'expected 1 to be +0' (zero-grant actor saw the full count). All mutations reverted; fix restored and reverified green before finalizing.

The first attempt at the new live DB test (ci/checks/db/report-page-render-read-pdp.db.test.ts) failed with the narrow actor seeing SUM=0 instead of 100 — root cause: my seed helper for choros."grant" rows omitted `confirmed_by`, and the NEWLY-wired getGrantsForSubject resolver (unlike the pre-existing application-level checkReadGrant inline query, which only checks role_assignment.confirmed_by) enforces T-0397's grant-level dual-control gate (`g.confirmed_by IS NOT NULL`, plus a critical-grant confirmed2_by check that a plain 'record read' grant does not trigger). Fixed by adding `confirmed_by: 'seed'` to both grant-seeding helpers — a useful reminder that report-page-render.ts's OWN inline authz query (defaultCheckReadGrant) is looser than the canonical getGrantsForSubject DAO on this exact point, though out of scope for this task to reconcile (both remain intentionally separate: application-level page gate vs record-level READ-PDP gate).

CHANGES_REQUESTED round (adversary opus, HIGH): closing only /render + /export was an incomplete fix — the sibling /data raw-row endpoint (dataFloor2) leaked identically (full data dump of every record + exact full-registry COUNT(*), gated only by the application-level checkReadGrant). This is the classic 'walled one column, left the adjacent one open' failure: my own /export comment even boasted 'no raw-row dump' while /data WAS a raw dump. Lesson: when adding a record-level READ-PDP gate to one read surface of a module, audit EVERY sibling read surface in the same module in the same pass — a security gate is only as strong as its leakiest peer endpoint. Fixed /data in a fix-forward commit (threaded resolveReadVisibility, per-row isRecordReadable, visible-only total_count) + audited the remaining route (/process-analytics — S3 telemetry, not a record surface, no change needed); both /data unit + DB tests are mutationally red before the fix.

The final SOLO fitness:db run (run 3, after the concurrent T-0638 worktree finished) came back with a single failure — cross_tenant.test.ts's 'seedRowForTable: unknown table user_pref' — which turned out to be a PRE-EXISTING base-branch infra gap (the user_pref table was added to known_tenant_tables.txt by T-0651 without a matching seedRowForTable case), entirely unrelated to T-0632. A background chip for it already existed (task_eb7d26ea). Notably every doc-pipeline file that had flaked under concurrent contention in the earlier runs passed cleanly solo — confirming the earlier failures were pure PG-contention flakes, not code defects.
known_gap_noted_not_fixed: defaultCheckReadGrant's own inline grant-fetch query (the FIRST, application-level gate) does not check `g.confirmed_by`/T-0397 dual-control on the grant row, unlike the canonical getGrantsForSubject DAO this task newly wires as the SECOND, record-level gate. This is a pre-existing asymmetry in report-page-render.ts, out of scope for T-0632 (which is scoped to closing the record-level gap, not auditing the pre-existing application-level gate's dual-control posture) — flagged here for a possible follow-up, not fixed in this diff to avoid scope creep on a security-fix PR.
